question: What is a stockinette primarily made of?

options.B: Woven canvas with heavy metal wires

explanation: A stockinette is manufactured as a seamless, tubular knitted material that can stretch to fit different body parts. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is a knitted structure preferred over a woven fabric for a stockinette?

options.A: It completely stops all blood circulation
options.B: It sticks permanently to the patient's skin
options.C: It repels water completely like a raincoat
options.D: It stretches easily to fit body curves smoothly

explanation: The knit stitch allows the fabric to expand and conform tightly to irregular body shapes without forming wrinkles. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of placing a stockinette under a cast?

options.A: To cure the underlying bone fracture quickly
options.B: To protect the skin from rough casting materials
options.C: To add extra weight to the broken limb
options.D: To make the cast dry much faster in the sun

explanation: The stockinette acts as a soft barrier preventing harsh plaster or fiberglass from rubbing directly against the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h2)

question: A patient with a new forearm cast says the rough edge of the plaster is scratching their wrist. What should have been done with the stockinette to prevent this?

options.A: Stretching the stockinette tighter across the fingers
options.B: Soaking the outer stockinette in warm saline
options.C: Folding the stockinette edges back over the cast ends
options.D: Applying adhesive tape over the outer plaster

explanation: Rolling the extra stockinette material back over the edges of the hardened cast creates a smooth, protective border that stops skin irritation. You've got this! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which stockinette material is best known for being highly breathable and absorbent?
explanation: Cotton stockinettes absorb moisture well and provide a soft, breathable layer against the skin. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why would a nurse select a synthetic, water-resistant stockinette for a patient?

options.A: To permanently glue the cast to the patient's skin
options.B: When the patient needs extra warmth in cold weather
options.C: To increase the weight of the injured extremity
options.D: When using a specialized waterproof casting system

explanation: Synthetic water-resistant stockinettes are paired with waterproof padding so patients can bathe or swim without ruining the cast. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h3)

question: What happens if a nurse chooses a stockinette that is too narrow for a patient's leg?

options.A: It will dissolve when the plaster gets wet
options.B: It can squeeze the limb and restrict blood circulation
options.C: It will automatically stretch to fit any size perfectly
options.D: It will fall off the leg before the cast is applied

explanation: An undersized stockinette acts like a tourniquet when stretched tightly over a limb, cutting off proper blood flow. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h4)

question: You are getting ready to put a stockinette on a patient's lower leg that has a small healing sore. What is the best first step for that wound?

options.A: Scrub the ulcer vigorously with iodine until it stops bleeding
options.B: Leave the wound completely uncovered so it can breathe under the cast
options.C: Apply antibiotic ointment directly to the stockinette fabric
options.D: Cover the ulcer with a sterile dressing before putting on the stockinette

explanation: Standard stockinettes are clean, but not sterile! Always cover open wounds with a sterile dressing first to keep your patient safe. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h4)

question: How much extra stockinette length should generally be cut beyond the planned cast area?
explanation: Leaving 10 to 15 centimeters of extra stockinette at both ends is necessary so the edges can be folded back over the cast later. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why must the patient's fingers or toes be left uncovered at the end of the application process?

options.A: To allow the nurse to check blood circulation and color
options.B: To let the fingernails grow without obstruction
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling too hot
options.D: To make it easier to paint the fingernails

explanation: Leaving digits exposed is vital for neurovascular checks, allowing healthcare workers to monitor temperature, color, and capillary refill. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the classic 5 Ps assessed during neurovascular checks?
explanation: The 5 Ps stand for Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, and Paralysis. Perspiration is not part of this assessment. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h6)

question: A patient with a leg cast complains of a sharp, burning pain in one spot underneath. What stockinette issue could be causing this?

options.A: The stockinette is too long at the top of the knee
options.B: The cotton material is absorbing too much fresh air
options.C: A wrinkle or fold in the stockinette causing pressure
options.D: The stockinette color is clashing with the plaster

explanation: Sharp, localized burning pain under a cast is a classic sign that a wrinkle or bunch in the stockinette is pressing hard into the skin. Smooth it out early! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h6)
